# 2026-07-11 Platform Runtime and External Goal Team

Status: independent boundary audit complete and implementation blocked on the corrected platform migration below. Dynamic expert-squad identity closure remains a prerequisite; platform generality and the legacy goal-team extraction are not yet accepted.

## TaskArtifact Store Slice (2026-07-15)

### Recall

- User requirement: continue the platform-runtime goal by replacing the fixed frontend-replica source/evidence topology with the canonical immutable `TaskArtifact` ABI, then run the real frontend-replica flow. Every future real task publication uses the already-running main backend and main database with exact model `hexin/gpt-5.5`; isolated databases are only for deterministic tests. Do not restart, stop, refresh, or otherwise operate the user's backend or Overlay.
- Acceptance: a package tool invocation with a real persisted Task/session/message/tool-part owner can stage, atomically publish, materialize, and read immutable Task-scoped artifacts; ordinary plugins receive no artifact authority. Staging and materialization are invocation-lifetime resources and are cleaned in `finally`. Published snapshots are verified before and after rename and every subsequent read/materialization. Task deletion settles execution, captures the project roots, then atomically rechecks terminal identity and deletes database rows before touching TaskArtifact files. After commit it directly removes every TaskArtifact root; cleanup failures are explicit committed-deletion diagnostics and must not imply that database rows were restored.
- Hard constraints: no fallback path, current/latest alias, URL identity, parent/reuse relation, global store, second lifecycle engine, host gate, hidden workflow state, inactive-package scan, or legacy `SourceSnapshot`/`WebClone` topology. All paths are underneath the canonical Task runtime root. Symlinks, junctions, hard links, special files, path traversal, portable-name violations, case collisions, manifest mismatch, cross-Task refs, stale handles, and use-after-close fail before artifact bytes are trusted.
- Current source read before implementation: `specs/current/architecture/04-extensions.md`, `packages/plugin/src/task-artifact.ts`, `packages/plugin/src/tool.ts`, `packages/opencorvus/src/tool/plugin-tool-host.ts`, `packages/opencorvus/src/tool/task-tool-execution-scope.ts`, `packages/opencorvus/src/expert-squad/prompt-profile-resolver.ts`, `packages/opencorvus/src/project/runtime-paths.ts`, `packages/opencorvus/src/project/task-runtime-root.ts`, `packages/opencorvus/src/task-api/index.ts`, and `packages/opencorvus/src/project/delete.ts`.
- Whole-repository grep: `TaskArtifact` started with one canonical plugin ABI and ABI/build-artifact tests but no committed store or host facade. `createPluginToolHost()` is consumed by ordinary `ToolRegistry` and projected package tools, so it remains command-only. `packageToolFromDefinition()` is the exact point where `resolvePackageTaskToolExecutionScope()` has already established invocation authority. `EngineService.deleteTask()` is the physical Task-row deletion owner; project deletion calls it before deleting the project `.opencorvus` directory. The final deletion call-point scan covers `deleteTask`, `deleteSession({deleteTasks:true})`, Project identity convergence, runtime paths, route error schemas and the generated SDK contract.
- Independent agent feedback retained after correction: reuse the existing Task tool invocation settlement instead of introducing authority leases. Bind artifact capability only to the resolved package-tool scope and revoke it before returning. Publication verifies staging inventory/hash/link shape, renames once, then verifies committed inventory/hash/link shape. Materialize/read require exact snapshot verification before and after their byte operation. Physical deletion uses the database as the only commit authority and performs direct post-commit artifact cleanup; it has no filesystem rollback protocol.
- Verification required before acceptance: focused store tests including concurrent independent publication, tamper/link/case/path/cross-Task/stale-handle failures and cleanup fault injection; package-host integration through the production resolver; Task deletion success, database failure with untouched artifacts, retry/replan ordering in both directions, session batch cleanup continuation, and post-commit cleanup failure; OpenCorvus/plugin typechecks; `git diff --check`; independent source review bound to the exact final tree; prefixed commit and push to `myhexin/v0.0.3beta` without staging parallel dashboard work.
- Implemented boundary: plugin `ToolHost` is now a mandatory `project`/`task` discriminated union. Ordinary plugins receive the frozen command-only project host. Only `packageToolFromDefinition()` after exact persisted invocation resolution receives a task host, and its TaskArtifact execution is always closed outside the package callback with primary/validation/cleanup failure aggregation. The committed snapshot identity and refs expose no persistent path; only execution-owned staging and materialization handles expose temporary filesystem paths.
- Implemented storage semantics: publication inventories strict portable single-link files, rejects empty directories and case collisions, writes a canonical manifest, verifies the complete staging root, performs one same-volume rename, and verifies the complete committed root. Read and materialize verify before and after byte access; close revalidates every materialized source and removes unpublished stages/materializations. Returned snapshot/manifest/ref graphs are deeply frozen.
- Implemented destruction semantics: `deleteTask` and `deleteSession({deleteTasks:true})` settle existing execution, capture exact project directories, then re-read every Task's identity and terminal status inside the row-deletion transaction. A winning retry/replan aborts deletion before filesystem work; a winning deletion makes a stale retry/replan update fail before dispatch. After commit, cleanup directly removes every `ta` root and continues across a batch before throwing `TaskArtifactDeletionCommittedError` with `committed:true`, exact Task IDs and failed root paths. There is no `ta-delete`, quarantine handle or restore path. Routes document settlement conflict and committed-cleanup responses; generated OpenAPI/SDK artifacts were refreshed.
- Whole-repository physical-delete correction: `ProjectGC` previously deleted Project rows by age and cascaded Tasks without settlement. This contradicted the recorded project-destruction architecture and would orphan Task runtime data, so age-based Project deletion and its CLI option were deleted. ProjectGC now removes only orphan snapshot/session-diff caches. Duplicate exact-worktree convergence now rejects a duplicate Project that already owns a TaskArtifact root rather than rewriting the Task project ID while leaving immutable manifests bound to the old identity.
- First independent exact-tree result: two reviewers returned `REJECT` despite the earlier green suite. They reproduced `close()` returning before an already-started stage/publication, publication through an ancestor junction, acceptance of noncanonical or manually constructed snapshots, and a quarantine rename whose post-rename verification failure left the Task row pointing at a missing root. They also identified a delete/recreate race, publication tampering that `close()` did not revalidate, `existsSync` fail-open Project convergence, missing `ta-delete` identity protection, an absolute materialization path returned through package-tool output, and Task deletion errors attached to `session.config.get` instead of `session.delete`. These findings supersede the earlier pending-review evidence and prove that it was false-green.
- Correction after rejection: every operation is registered before its first asynchronous boundary; close revokes new calls, awaits the exact in-flight set, revalidates every successful publication/materialization source, and then cleans execution-owned paths. Managed directory creation and verification walk every ancestor and reject links; inventories compare directory entries before and after traversal. Canonical manifest bytes and a strict Store-owned internal publication receipt are required. A terminal Task rejects new artifact operations. Quarantine now constructs its restoration handle before rename and restores the current root if post-rename verification fails. Duplicate Project convergence fails closed on filesystem inspection and treats both `ta` and `ta-delete` as immutable identity ownership. Package-tool output now returns artifact bytes rather than a materialization directory; the host-side test inspects the canonical runtime root after callback cleanup.
- Corrected executable evidence before round-two review: Store tests pass 16/16 with 31 assertions, including concurrent close, ancestor junction, mid-inventory addition, canonical-byte, unpublished-snapshot and terminal-Task negatives. Production resolver TaskArtifact execution passes with no filesystem path in tool output. Task/deleteSession quarantine and rollback plus full Project identity and generated SDK contract pass 55/55 with 239 assertions. OpenCorvus typecheck, official SDK generation, API documentation generation, route inventory across 30 files and `git diff --check` pass. Generated OpenAPI proves `TaskCancellationIncompleteError` and `TaskArtifactDeletionCommittedError` belong to `session.delete` and are absent from both session config operations. A fresh exact-tree attack and full-slice review are still required, so this slice remains unaccepted and no real Task has been published.
- Round-two review correction after user challenge: both reviewers returned `REJECT`, but their findings mixed two different trust models. The installed-extension decision already recorded below is authoritative: explicitly installed package tools are trusted executable extensions in the host process and have filesystem/command capabilities; this runtime does not claim resistance to a malicious same-process package or hostile concurrent filesystem rewrites. Providing that property requires a separate process and capability broker, not more in-process scans, receipts, ledgers or cleanup states. The self-asserted `.publication.json` cannot prove Store provenance and is deleted; canonical manifest, exact identity, inventory and digest remain the only cooperative integrity source. No publication database ledger, signature layer, cleanup claim state, lifecycle mutex subsystem or additional `readdir` loop will be introduced.
- Round-two findings retained as real platform defects: deletion must reuse the existing managed-ancestor check so an accidental/pre-existing Task-root junction cannot operate outside the project; physical deletion must re-read the Task inside its database transaction and refuse a Task legitimately reopened by retry/replan during settlement; canonical ABI record keys and case-insensitive path prefixes must compose consistently across standalone and manifest schemas; and a task-scoped package host must revoke and settle every started `runCommand` together with TaskArtifact operations. Tests must cover those four production paths. The reviewers' adversarial same-process snapshot forgery and path replacement cases remain evidence that this is not a sandbox, not requirements for an in-process security mechanism.
- Round-three correction after the over-abstraction challenge: the accepted round-two deletion order was still false-green. It renamed `ta` to `ta-delete` before the database decision, so a legitimate retry/replan could reopen and dispatch a package tool that recreated `ta`; the database recheck then correctly rejected deletion, but restoration could not replace the newly occupied root and stranded the old immutable artifacts in `ta-delete`. The root cause is attempting to simulate a cross-filesystem/database transaction. The corrected single-source order is: capture each Task project directory, atomically re-read terminal identity and delete database rows in one database transaction, then perform best-effort TaskArtifact cleanup after commit. If retry/replan updates first, deletion rejects before touching artifacts; if deletion commits first, the stale update finds no Task and never dispatches. The pre-commit quarantine/restore protocol, its handle type, and rollback tests are obsolete and must be deleted. Post-commit cleanup attempts every Task and reports the existing committed-deletion error with exact residue paths. Independent source review accepted this smaller architecture and found no reason for a new lock, ownership protocol, state machine, ledger, receipt or scan layer.
- Round-three executable closure: the four-file production correction is a net deletion of 166 lines (24 additions and 190 deletions); `ta-delete`, its runtime-path API, handle type and current tests have zero live source matches. Deterministic regressions pause retry and replan only after their real Task/session lineage read, allow `deleteTask` or batch `deleteSession` to commit, then prove the stale update fails before the production dispatch binding is called. The inverse ordering proves retry/replan abort deletion before artifact cleanup; database rollback leaves roots untouched; committed batch cleanup continues after one failure. The deletion suite passes 12/12 with 47 assertions, the Store suite passes 15/15 after removing its unrelated Git-repository fixture, the combined ABI/Store/host/delete/runtime/error/SDK run passes 95/95 with 316 assertions, the Project identity regression passes 1/1, OpenCorvus typecheck and `git diff --check` pass. Earlier broad runs were invalidated only by the known Windows Git supervisor/read-tree resource failure and were rerun on the same product tree without unnecessary Git fixtures. Two exact-tree independent reviewers returned `ACCEPT`; neither found a remaining product race, current-document double source, fallback, gate, lock, ledger, receipt or state-machine addition.

## Recall

### User Request

- Verify that OpenCorvus is genuinely platform and infrastructure oriented: core should provide only a general development runtime and extend agent-team behavior through general interfaces and protocols.
- Audit abstraction quality, extensibility, stability, and foreseeable bottlenecks, then remove proven architectural and legacy debt rather than documenting it as accepted risk.
- Reimplement the existing goal-oriented requirements, architecture, build, integrity, research, review, and orchestration team as a complete external expert squad using the new dynamic-agent package projection.
- After the external package works through the real runtime, remove the legacy team configuration and prompt sources from core instead of retaining two implementations.
- Simulate a real user starting the backend and frontend, selecting and running the external team, and verify the complete observable chain without hidden failures.
- Preserve the preceding dynamic-identity objective: `capability_projection.agents.<agentID>` is runtime identity, while `base_role` is only a core runtime-template seed.
- After the platform boundary is independently finalized, provide an expert-squad development SDK and concise human-readable documentation so agents can author new squads through the final schema and protocol without duplicating registry, validation, packaging, or release logic.
- The latest E2E directive supersedes the earlier `goal-development` text-file smoke as the final user simulation: run the real `frontend-replica` project package with the exact model `hexin/gpt-5.5`, complete a real source-bound webpage replica, and verify its rendered desktop result through the full Mission/Task/agent/preview/evidence chain.
- The user simulation itself is fully automatic after publication: the driver selects the squad/model and submits one natural replica task only. Source research, consent/state preparation, screenshots, agent selection/order, implementation and evidence creation belong to the expert squad; the driver may observe and independently verify them but must not prebuild their inputs or execute their workflow.
- During the real E2E, the observer only polls the scheduler's publicly visible messages, tool results, Task status and preview/evidence at intervals. It must not choose agents, order dispatches, inject context or artifacts, trigger retries, operate the source site, advance a workflow, or otherwise micromanage the scheduler. A visible defect is recorded with its evidence; source correction happens only after that run naturally fails or terminates, followed by a newly published Task.
- The final user simulation must run through an observable GUI so the user can watch the real chain. Use the existing main backend and main database with Node-launched headed Playwright/Chrome against the real Overlay; retain the live address, task-scoped screenshots and diagnostics. Headless-only, API-only or report-only execution is not acceptance.

### Acceptance Criteria

1. Core owns only reusable development-runtime protocols and implementations: sessions, streaming model calls, task/message/artifact persistence, scheduler lifecycle, exact dispatch, runtime-template resolution, tool execution, skill/MCP projection, and observable error delivery.
2. Team identity, worker inventory, labels, collaboration topology, role instructions, domain prompts, skill grants, package tools, MCP refs, and selection guidance have one source in an external expert-squad package.
3. The legacy goal-development team is represented by non-base-role dynamic agent IDs. At minimum its requirements, architecture, implementation, integrity, research, fact-check, workload, intent, exploration, visual, and scheduler responsibilities are complete where the current production team exposes those responsibilities.
4. Selecting the package through `prompt_profile.active` is sufficient to project scheduler and worker capabilities. No built-in profile, hidden session state, hard-coded runtime-ID list, alias, or inactive-package scan participates.
5. `base_role` selects a reusable execution contract only. Core role contracts must not encode package-specific team membership, routing order, collaboration policy, user-domain policy, or package prompt text.
6. Package removal or inactive selection removes the team projection. Missing agent IDs, resources, runtime templates, tools, skills, MCP providers, and terminal contracts fail explicitly.
7. The external team executes through the existing generic `dispatch_agent`, runner, message, A2A, catalog, mount, payload, and template protocols. It must not introduce a second workflow engine or package-defined host state machine.
8. After the package passes, obsolete core prompt/config/team-topology sources and their tests are deleted. There is no compatibility parser, built-in alias, duplicate workflow, or shadow prompt source.
9. Extensibility review covers adding a new dynamic agent, sharing one base role across agents, new package skill/tool/MCP grants, remote agent/protocol evolution, projection hashing/cache invalidation, cancellation, concurrent sessions, and version/schema evolution without name guessing.
10. Stability review covers first-request initialization, lease re-entry, config invalidation, streaming, terminal failure visibility, cancellation, package isolation, concurrent same-base-role workers, cache invalidation, and frontend/backend contract drift.
11. The existing main backend, main database and real Overlay frontend are used without restarting, stopping, refreshing or otherwise disturbing the user's running OpenCorvus/overlay. Node-launched headed Playwright/Chrome exposes the GUI for user observation and verifies project/package discovery, selection, catalog, settings, dispatch-visible messages, tool/skill/MCP projections, failure surfaces, and terminal evidence. The live address and task-scoped evidence are retained, and screenshots are inspected manually.
12. Focused and full tests, typecheck, generated artifact freshness, document health, dead-code checks, `git diff --check`, independent source reviews, commit, and push to `myhexin/v0.0.3beta` all pass.
13. The expert-squad development SDK is implemented only after the runtime protocol is finalized. It reuses the production manifest schema, registry, package manager, provider-ref naming, and validation paths; exposes typed package authoring/scaffolding, validation, packaging, and explicit provisioning APIs; includes a short human guide and one concrete example; and does not introduce a second schema, loader, active-squad source, compatibility layer, or hidden workflow DSL.
14. The final real E2E selects and runs `frontend-replica` with the exact configured model `hexin/gpt-5.5`. It starts from a real public source URL and freshly captured source evidence, produces a runnable local target and task-scoped preview/evidence, exercises desktop interactions and keyboard focus, captures and manually inspects source/target/Overlay screenshots, proves the package's dynamic agent identities and Mission child-result reconciliation, and rejects a text-file-only, mocked, fixture-only, screenshot-string, hidden-iframe, or unrendered result.

### Hard Constraints

- No fallback, compatibility alias, second active-squad field, hidden message, synthetic state, keyword routing, host gate, or package-defined workflow/state machine.
- Preserve the current external-squad schema replacement in place; do not create a v1/v2 compatibility branch.
- Do not mistake a renamed hard-coded role list for a general protocol. A retained core specialization needs evidence that it is reusable runtime infrastructure rather than team configuration.
- Do not move trusted host internals into arbitrary package code merely to reduce core file count. External packages use explicit, least-authority package tool/skill/MCP and dispatch protocols.
- Do not delete generated SDK/OpenAPI or unrelated application code based only on line counts. Deletion requires reachability, provenance, replacement, and regression evidence.
- Do not create worktrees or restart, refresh, kill, or reuse the user's running OpenCorvus/overlay process. User simulation uses the already running main backend, main database and Overlay without process intervention.
- All tests that can wait on processes use stdout/stderr inactivity timeouts; frontend Playwright runs under Node.
- Every implementation slice receives independent-agent review before acceptance.
- The E2E model is an exact provider/model identity, not a same-name search: `hexin/gpt-5.5` must resolve from the supplied catalog and credential source or fail before launching the chain. The harness must not guess another provider, print credentials, or fall back to the previous DeepSeek run.
- The E2E driver publishes one natural user task and observes the resulting public records. It must not pre-capture the source, dismiss source-site consent, open source controls, seed task artifacts, dispatch workers or encode agent order on behalf of the selected squad.
- The final GUI E2E is visible and headed. A headless browser, direct-API-only driver, mocked Overlay, temporary iframe or report without a real observable GUI cannot satisfy the user simulation.
- The frontend-replica E2E is desktop-only unless the user separately requests multi-device migration. A historical benchmark prompt mentioning tablet/mobile does not authorize those deliverables.

| UI/runtime proof           | Overlay catalog/settings tests cover dynamic projections, but no current test simulates selecting and executing the external legacy team from a fresh user startup. | Use the existing main backend/database and Node Playwright evidence against real APIs and rendered UI without restarting the running processes.                                                   |

### Independent Agent Feedback

- The independent platform audit blocked the current architecture. Dynamic IDs now identify workers, but the closed twelve-adapter set, built-in General team, WorkflowRegistry, static PromptProfile targets, and host-authored next-agent guidance still make core own the legacy team topology.
- `Agent.Info` currently mixes primary assistants, helpers, scheduler, runtime templates, and free custom agents. Config discovery additionally scans `agent/`, `agents/`, `mode/`, and `modes/`. These are separate agent-definition paths beside expert-squad projections and must not remain an implicit agent-team extension surface.
- `base_role` is still the final model/operator-prompt configuration identity: runner model resolution and prompt append read `config.agent[baseRole]`, so two same-base-role dynamic agents cannot receive independent operator runtime configuration. Runtime override identity must be `(squadID, agentID)`, layered after the required base template and package projection.
- The worker descriptor/projection hash does not bind the effective core/package/operator system-prompt digest or explicit template/adapter ABI version. Continuations can therefore reuse the same descriptor hash after effective behavior changes; this must fail explicitly instead.
- Historical audit finding, superseded by the explicit installed-extension trust decision at the manifest v1 package-tool execution Recall below: package-tool abstract-syntax-tree import filtering is not a sandbox, and project packages execute trusted code in the host process with declared Node-core and projected host capabilities. A restricted broker/isolated process remains the only acceptable design for a future **untrusted-code** runtime, but direct host execution is the accepted single path for explicitly installed trusted package tools.
- Legacy role configuration is partly dead: requirements/architect/frontend-design/intent-analysis/build `max_steps` have no production reader. `assistant.acceptance_visual` feeds production-unreachable metric code. These fields must be deleted, not migrated into the external package.
- Core role prompts cannot be deleted mechanically because existing domain packages intentionally carry small deltas over typed runtime-template operational seeds. Core may retain only input shape, private-tool ABI, terminal finalizer, permission boundary, and data-integrity instructions. Team membership, ordering, redispatch, next-action, goal-count, and domain policy belong only in the active package.
- The current `general` manifest projects the entire legacy team under IDs equal to their base roles. General must become scheduler plus a minimal non-base-role developer projection; the complete team moves to `goal-development` with exact dynamic IDs.
- The server review already found a reusable-runtime stability defect: first-request global config mutation recursively acquired an instance read lease while holding the same entry's initialization writer. The accepted direction is inherited same-key lease reuse in `Instance.forEachActive`, with a first-request regression rather than request prewarming.

## Corrected Platform Boundary

### Runtime Registries

| Authority                  | Owns                                                                                                                                              | Must not own                                                                                                      |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `PrimaryAssistantRegistry` | Product-facing Coding, Chat, Mission, and Control sessions.                                                                                       | Helpers, host scheduler identity, runtime templates, expert-squad worker inventory, or dynamic dispatch identity. |
| `HelperAgentRegistry`      | Internal Title, Summary, and Compaction model/prompt slots.                                                                                       | Product assistants, host identity, worker templates, or expert-squad identity.                                    |
| `RuntimeTemplateRegistry`  | Core prompt seed, model default, base tools, permission/source boundary, session contract, finalizer and adapter reference.                       | Team label, team membership, collaboration order, domain policy, or active identity.                              |
| `DispatchAdapterRegistry`  | Input schema, dispatcher, continuation contract, terminal output, typed persistence and ABI version for trusted host operations.                  | Dynamic target literals, next-agent policy, workflow order, skip/retry policy, or package identity.               |
| `PromptProfileResolver`    | One frozen `ResolvedProjectedAgent` per `(squadID, agentID)`, including template/adapter ABI, effective prompt/model/tools/skills/MCP and hashes. | Static base-role target catalog, inactive scans, or name aliases.                                                 |
| Active package             | Scheduler instructions, dynamic worker inventory, labels, role/team prompts and explicitly projected resources.                                   | Host workflow, state machine, session kind, finalizer, trusted adapter implementation, or hidden state.           |

### Required Migration Order

1. Add a core-owned generic delegated-worker runtime template/adapter for external roles that do not require a specialized typed persistence adapter. Keep specialized adapters only as reusable typed host capabilities.
2. Split primary/helper agents from runtime templates and make `base_role` resolve only through `RuntimeTemplateRegistry`. Remove free `mode/modes` aliases and prevent standalone custom-agent discovery from acting as a team-worker source.
3. Make dispatch adapter definitions the sole source of schema, implementation, continuation, private finalizer/tool ABI and version. Delete the parallel private-tool table and duplicate base-runtime diagnostic projection.
4. Make effective runtime overrides explicit: base-template operator override, then package projection, then `expert_squads.<squadID>.agents.<agentID>.runtime`. Missing or invalid layers fail; there is no same-name fallback.
5. Bind template ABI, adapter ABI and the exact effective system-prompt digest into the worker descriptor/projection hash.
6. Replace built-in General with scheduler plus a minimal dynamic developer. Add the complete external `goal-development` source package and payload using non-base-role IDs for every legacy responsibility.
7. Remove `WorkflowRegistry`, built-in/custom workflow config, workflow-selected/step shadow projections and fixed scheduler routing prose. Real sessions, outcomes, artifacts and goal runs remain the observable progress sources.
8. Remove static PromptProfile `builtIns`, `targets`, `overlayFor` and legacy compose paths. Built-in General loads through the registry; all runtime prompt composition consumes a resolved scheduler/worker capability.
9. Strip core prompt/tool/stage result text to operational facts and ABI instructions. Move goal-team collaboration and next-agent policy to the external package scheduler and worker prompts using exact dynamic IDs.
10. Replace host-process package tool execution with a least-authority execution boundary before treating packages as a platform extension mechanism.

## Investigation Plan

1. Close all known dynamic-identity review blockers so the platform audit starts from one coherent projection model.
2. Produce a source-by-source ledger for core runtime ABI versus legacy team configuration, including every role, prompt, model slot, private tool, stage adapter, workflow reference, catalog surface, and test.
3. Define the smallest reusable worker-template and scheduler protocol that can host the existing team without package-defined workflow/state machinery or trusted-host leakage.

### Dispatch Adapter Authority Recall

- Independent read-only audit confirms `DispatchAdapterContractRegistry` is currently metadata-only. `orchestrator/tools.ts` separately enumerates thirteen schemas in `SchedulerDispatchTargetInputSchemas`, reflects `Partial` handlers from `tools[id]?.execute`, and therefore detects a missing unprojected adapter only when an active package happens to use it.
- Completion semantics are also duplicated: stage modules and Build/Delegated Worker paths repeat session/finalizer literals, `RuntimeTemplateRegistry` copies adapter-owned session/private-tool/finalizer/continuation fields, and `AgentRoleContract` copies the twelve worker templates again.
- `schedulerWorkflowToolName(baseRole)` is a forbidden reverse lookup from template seed to dispatch adapter. Adapter implementations must know their adapter ID; dynamic execution identity must arrive as the exact required projected `agentID`, never be recovered from an optional tool-options side channel.
- The accepted target is a pure adapter definition containing schema plus discriminated completion ABI, and a composition-root binder that requires an exhaustive executor record. The bound registry becomes the single schema/executor/completion authority used by `dispatch_agent`.
- To avoid a dependency cycle, pure contract/schema code cannot import runner, Orchestrator, or stage implementations. Implementations depend on the contract and are injected by `tools.ts`; the registry never imports implementations.
- Safe migration order is: completion/continuation ABI and RuntimeTemplate duplication; schema authority plus exhaustive binder; explicit executor context with required dynamic `agentID`; AgentRoleContract worker deletion; then WorkflowRegistry/config/event/board removal.

### Validation Discipline

- Bun tests run with `--timeout=0` behind `script/run-with-inactivity.ts`; the external wrapper is the sole timeout and is refreshed by stdout/stderr activity.
- Test, typecheck, formatting, and diff-check commands must run as separate shell commands. Chaining a failing test followed by a successful diff check causes the shell to report only the final command's status and is not accepted evidence.

### 2026-07-12 Windows Supervisor Test-Protocol Recall

- User requirement retained: the platform runtime and its validation tools must be reliable before the remaining expert-squad extraction, legacy cleanup, real end-to-end verification, and SDK work can be accepted. Test infrastructure defects must be repaired at their source and cannot be hidden with retries, fallback helpers, longer startup waits, or serialization gates.
- Acceptance for this slice: every Windows fake helper in `shell.test.ts` speaks the current atomic `ready.json` protocol with exact request, helper, and target identities; lifecycle mocks settle `exited` when disposal succeeds; startup-failure assertions use current readiness terminology; the complete shell supervisor file, real Process supervisor paths, Architect, and Integrity files pass without leaving new supervisor request directories.
- Hard constraints: do not change production supervisor semantics without a production failure reproduction; do not infer readiness from process exit; do not restore `pid_file`; do not touch unrelated or user-owned OpenCorvus/Overlay processes; do not delete historical temporary directories until ownership is proved.
- Sources reread: this record; `specs/records/2026-06/2026-06-25-windows-supervisor-worktree-lock.md`; `src/shell/process-supervisor.ts`; `src/util/process.ts`; `src/shell/shell.ts`; the Rust native helper; `test/shell.test.ts`; `test/util/process.test.ts`; `engine/git.ts`; and the fixture project bootstrap.
- Whole-repository searches covered `ProcessSupervisor.spawnCommand`, `ProcessSupervisor.spawnShell`, `handle.dispose`, `ready_file`, `pid_file`, `waitForReadyMarker`, `ensureGitignore`, and isolated Git index commands. The first search scope incorrectly omitted `test/util/process.test.ts`; the corrected inventory contains stale fake helpers in both `shell.test.ts` and `util/process.test.ts` and no production `pid_file` reader.
- Evidence before edits: the local debug helper is the only resolved helper and is fresh; 100 concurrent real `Process.run(["git", "--version"])` calls passed with zero new request directories; complete Architect and Integrity files passed with zero new request directories. The complete shell file failed 10 of 33 tests: eight fake helpers wrote removed `request.pid_file` or asserted retired PID wording, and two mocked handles reported successful disposal without ever settling their `exited` promise.
- Independent audit feedback: the Rust helper can return a target exit code only after atomically publishing the ready marker; pre-readiness native failures return 125 with stderr. Therefore the earlier transient `exit=1`/missing-marker observation is not sufficient evidence for a production polling change. The audit also found three reproducible ownership escapes independent of that observation: `plugin-tool-host.ts` propagates termination failure before disposal, while the already-aborted foreground paths in `tool/bash.ts` and `session/shell-exec.ts` await termination outside their disposal `try/finally`. These paths require direct behavioral regressions.

| Call point                                                      | Disposition                                                                                                                                                       |
| --------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `shell.test.ts` fake helpers writing `request.pid_file`         | Replace with exact protocol-1 JSON written to `request.ready_file`, including `request_id`, wrapper helper PID, and target PID.                                   |
| `util/process.test.ts` fake helpers writing `request.pid_file`  | Use the same canonical fake-marker source and retain fast-output coverage under the current protocol.                                                             |
| Readiness race tests                                            | Preserve their race purpose using the atomic marker path and current error terminology.                                                                           |
| Live-handle disposal mocks                                      | Settle `exited` as part of successful disposal so they model the required handle contract.                                                                        |
| `plugin-tool-host.ts` termination failure                       | Always dispose and await output closure; preserve the primary termination error and combine it with cleanup failure evidence.                                     |
| Foreground `tool/bash.ts` and `session/shell-exec.ts` pre-abort | Move the initial termination await inside the existing disposal `try/finally`; prove a termination error cannot skip disposal.                                    |
| Production Rust supervisor core                                 | Replace the post-creation assignment window with atomic creation-time Job membership; retain the ready-marker ordering and no-retry TypeScript polling semantics. |
| Historical `%TEMP%` directories                                 | Record as cleanup debt; do not mass-delete while active/user ownership is unknown.                                                                                |

#### Implementation and calibration

The independent review separated two previously conflated observations. A helper returning a target exit code proves that it had published readiness, while a suspended orphan proves that some target never reached `ResumeThread`; without matching `request_id`, helper process identifier, and target process identifier they cannot be assigned to one request. The structural orphan window was nevertheless real: post-creation `AssignProcessToJobObject` left a created suspended target outside Job ownership if the helper itself terminated between those calls.

The native helper now creates the target with `STARTUPINFOEXW` and `PROC_THREAD_ATTRIBUTE_JOB_LIST`, so Job membership and process creation are one Windows kernel operation. The attribute-list resource owns both its aligned storage and the boxed Job-handle array because Microsoft requires the attribute value to remain alive until `DeleteProcThreadAttributeList`; an initial implementation incorrectly kept that array on the stack and the native test exposed it as Win32 error 6 before it was corrected. The Job handle itself remains non-inheritable so the target cannot keep its own kill-on-close owner alive. Microsoft primary references: `https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/desktop/api/processthreadsapi/nf-processthreadsapi-updateprocthreadattribute`, `https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/jobapi2/nf-jobapi2-createjobobjectw`, and `https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/procthread/job-objects`.

The TypeScript supervisor now includes the request identity, helper process identifier, and ready-marker path in startup failures. Plugin tool commands unconditionally perform bounded disposal and output closure even when termination fails. Foreground Bash and SessionShell pre-abort paths feed termination into the same observed race and disposal `finally`, avoiding both skipped disposal and an unobserved secondary rejection. Background Bash owns one disposal promise; natural or failed exit clears the lease and initiates immediate disposal, while the lease exists only for a still-live owner.

Validation after correction uses the repository's required inactivity wrapper and disables Bun's default elapsed test timeout: `bun packages/opencorvus/script/run-with-inactivity.ts --inactivity-ms 120000 -- bun test --timeout=0 ...`. Earlier direct `bun test` runs were invalid because Bun's default five-second elapsed timeout killed child processes and printed `killed dangling process`; the resulting helper and target exit-code failures were test-runner termination, not a supervisor retry condition. Under the canonical command, the native drop-before-resume test passes 1/1; the complete shell, Process, Architect, Integrity, plugin-host, and SessionShell combination passes 81/81 with 325 assertions and zero new `opencorvus-supervisor-*` directories; the complete Bash file passes 37/37 with 117 assertions; and OpenCorvus package typecheck passes. The strict readiness tests cover incorrect request identity, helper identity, protocol, target process identifier, and extra fields through real spawn/cleanup paths. After three corrective review rounds covering timer re-arm, pre-abort lease creation, rejected background exit, readiness-window abort, and abort cleanup rejection, the independent reviewer returned `ACCEPT`.

#### Correction implementation and local calibration

The correction removes the four blockers instead of retaining transitional behavior:

- `PromptProfileResolver` now obtains one declaration-only project snapshot, validates every configured `skill_mounts` and `expert_squads` identity against the exact manifest keys, checks the manifest declaration hash before loading the active package, and resolves the active scheduler plus every projected worker. Inactive packages do not load README prompt content, selector content, tools, skills, MCP providers, or package libraries during configuration validation.
- Project config, session overlays, Mission profile selection, and Global config call the canonical projection validator before persistence. `GlobalInfo` omits project-owned `skill_mounts` and `expert_squads`; the merged on-disk Global document is also validated so a new request cannot hide a stale project-owned field. Unknown nested `tool_permissions` keys are rejected instead of being dropped.
- Config- and Skill-dependent HTTP surfaces expose structured `ConfigInvalidError` and `SkillInvalidError` 400 responses. The formal OpenAPI generator, JavaScript SDK generator, and English/Chinese API documentation generator own the checked-in artifacts.
- Task creation owns its complete unpublished materialization. The root session is created with config overlay, effective-config snapshot, and permissions in one row; attachment writes remain pending until the task, initial progress, channel binding, and user-request note commit in one Database transaction; the IntentBundle and candidate session are removed on failure. Attachment rollback uses the exact `<sha>.<ext>` reference and concurrent pending-write ownership, so a persisted blob with another extension neither retains nor loses the candidate. Same-project duplicate `requestID` values serialize through an unambiguous tuple key before materialization.
- Mission profile changes use one Mission-scoped lease through wake. Unknown profiles do not create a Mission row, overlay, or runtime directory; wake failure restores the previous profile; concurrent profile changes cannot expose one request's projection to another. Cleanup failures preserve both the primary and rollback errors.
- The combined test run exposed a separate test-order defect: `response-language.test.ts` installed permanent, incomplete Bun module replacements and `mock.restore()` could not undo them, so later attachment tests lost `Instance.provide`. Production now calls the pure `SystemPrompt.withResponseLanguage` composition source and the test has no module mocks. The original contaminated combination failed with 65 passes and 21 failures; the same response-language-before-attachment order then passed 24 tests with 70 assertions.

#### Second independent review and materialization correction

The fresh exact-tree review returned `NOT ACCEPT` despite all focused tests passing. It found two production paths that the previous tests did not exercise:

1. `recoverTaskByRequest` identified the request unique constraint by matching SQLite error message and column-name text. The in-process owner lock cannot cover another process or an external Database writer, so this keyword rule was both prohibited and load-bearing.
2. Physical attachment and metadata writes marked ownership only after `fs.writeFile` resolved. A write that created or partially wrote the destination and then rejected could leave bytes behind before `beginWrite` returned a rollback lease.

The correction uses structured and atomic authorities. `Database.hasSqliteCode` walks the real error/cause/AggregateError graph and accepts the exact `SQLITE_CONSTRAINT_UNIQUE` code; recovery then requires the exact durable project/request row. This is unambiguous because `persistQueuedTask` inserts `engine_task` before every other unique surface in its transaction. A real route regression inserts the competing task after candidate IntentBundle materialization but before task persistence; the SQLite constraint fires, the existing task ID is returned, and the abandoned session, attachment, IntentBundle, and task row are absent.

Attachment blob and metadata bytes now write to a unique same-directory pending file and publish through an exclusive hard link. Publication failure or any later cleanup failure removes only files owned by that attempt and preserves the primary error. Two fault-injection regressions write partial blob/metadata temp bytes and then throw an `EIO` I/O error; both leave the attachment directory empty. Existing pending-write, exact-extension, shared-commit, all-rollback, sweep, and response-language test-order behavior remains intact.

Post-correction evidence: the complete Task route file passes 19 tests with 100 assertions; the complete attachment write file passes 11 tests with 22 assertions; Task/Mission/request-owner passes 64 tests with 292 assertions; response-language plus attachment write/sweep passes 26 tests with 74 assertions. OpenCorvus and JavaScript SDK typechecks, `api:routes-check`, `docs:check`, and the production residue scan for message-based request-conflict matching pass. A third exact-tree independent review is required before commit.

#### Third independent review and cross-process attachment authority

The third exact-tree review returned `NOT ACCEPT`. The structured SQLite request-conflict recovery is accepted, but the attachment implementation is not: `pendingWriteStates` proves ownership only inside one process, a publisher can delete a final hard link after another process has adopted it, metadata failure can remove a concurrently adopted blob, and sweep still uses a 60-second age guess while swallowing Windows `EBUSY` / `EPERM` and `stat` errors. Those paths can lose a valid attachment, delete only one member of the blob/metadata pair, and report a deletion that did not happen.

The corrected authority is one SQLite `attachment_write_lease` row per materialization attempt plus one lease-owned directory under the project attachment root. `beginWrite` inserts the lease before touching or adopting a final path. The lease remains visible for the whole gap between filesystem publication and a durable reference. Task creation removes its attachment leases in the same SQLite transaction that inserts the task attachment references; before commit, other processes see the leases, and after commit they see the durable references. Rollback and sweep acquire the SQLite write lock before reading references or peer leases, so a new adopter cannot appear between the ownership decision and filesystem deletion.

The physical contract is:

1. A lease directory owns its unique pending bytes. Final blob and metadata paths are shared content-addressed objects as soon as they are linked; a publisher never infers exclusive final-path ownership from having created the link.
2. Only a writer holding the SQLite write transaction may remove a final pair, and only when no durable reference and no other lease exist. A failed pair deletion restores every already removed member and propagates the filesystem error; Windows sharing errors are never converted to success.
3. `sweep` reconciles durable references and lease rows before enumerating orphans. A referenced lease is settled. An unreferenced lease is reclaimed only when its owner is on the current host and its process identifier is proven absent; a live or remote owner remains protected. Unknown pending or garbage-collection residue is an explicit integrity error.
4. `listOnDisk` propagates `stat` failures. The age heuristic, `utimes` refresh, process-local ownership state, and silent delete retry are deleted rather than retained as compatibility behavior.

Whole-repository call-point inventory for this correction:

```powershell
rg -n "AttachmentStore|beginWrite|PendingWrite|sweepProject|listOnDisk|GC_MIN_AGE_MS|pendingWriteStates|AttachmentWriteLeaseTable|attachmentPending" packages/opencorvus/src packages/opencorvus/test specs/current specs/records/2026-07
rg -n "persistQueuedTask|recoverTaskByRequest|requestID|attachments" packages/opencorvus/src/engine packages/opencorvus/src/task-api packages/opencorvus/test/server packages/opencorvus/test/engine
rg -n "AttachmentStore\.write\(" packages/opencorvus/src packages/opencorvus/test
```

| Call point                                          | Disposition                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| --------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `AttachmentStore.beginWrite`                        | Replace process-local counters with the SQLite lease row and lease directory. Return explicit transaction preparation, post-commit confirmation, and rollback operations.                                                                                                                                                                  |
| `persistQueuedTask`                                 | Accept the pending attachment handles and delete their lease rows inside the task/reference transaction. The task row remains the first write so request-ID conflict recovery stays unambiguous.                                                                                                                                           |
| `EngineService.createTaskInner`                     | Pass pending handles into `persistQueuedTask`, confirm only after the transaction returns, and roll back candidates on every failure including a real competing request-ID writer.                                                                                                                                                         |
| `AttachmentStore.write` production callers          | Retain a live lease because these callers return a reference before their enclosing session/tool/artifact owner is persisted. Sweep may settle it when a durable reference is visible, but cannot guess an unreferenced live writer is abandoned. A later slice must make each owner transaction explicit before removing this protection. |
| `AttachmentStore.sweep` / `Instance.provide`        | Replace age-based collection with reference-plus-lease reconciliation under a SQLite write transaction, strict pending residue validation, and paired deletion.                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `AttachmentStore.listOnDisk` and route/read helpers | Preserve exact `<sha>.<ext>` identity and metadata validation; propagate filesystem inspection errors.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| Attachment write/sweep and Task route tests         | Add cross-lease adoption, last-rollback, task transaction handoff, dead-owner reclamation, live-owner protection, partial write, Windows delete failure, `stat` failure, and unknown pending residue regressions.                                                                                                                          |

This correction is limited to the attachment/materialization authority needed by the exact runtime-identity slice. It does not accept the overall platform goal or the remaining host-owned Goal Development topology.

##### Pre-implementation design review: preceding lease design superseded

The independent reviewer rejected the preceding implementation plan before production edits. The SQLite lease table cannot be treated as a worktree-wide authority until the physical attachment root is bound to the exact Database UUID and project identity: two ordinary server processes using different `OPENCORVUS_HOME` values otherwise have different SQLite files but the same worktree blob paths. The root binding must be claimed and validated before the first blob, metadata, pending, or garbage-collection path is touched; a different authority fails explicitly rather than scanning or adopting the store.

The corrected process and transaction contract is stricter:

- A lease records a full `att_*` identifier, Database UUID, project ID, machine-incarnation token, process-incarnation token, process start time, and process identifier. Hostname is diagnostic only. A lease is dead only after an exact registered incarnation mismatch or an `ESRCH` (Error, No Such Process) probe. `EPERM` (Error, Operation Not Permitted), an unknown probe error, a different machine token, or missing proof preserves the lease and reports the uncertainty.
- Lease directories use the validated full lease ID. `Identifier.directoryKey()` is a short hash and is forbidden for ownership paths because it is not injective.
- `retain(tx)` receives the caller's active transaction, verifies that the exact `/attachment/<projectID>/<sha>.<ext>` reference is already present in that transaction, removes the private lease directory, and then deletes the lease row. It never opens a nested transaction. The caller confirms retention only after the outer transaction returns; an outer rollback restores the row and is followed by explicit attachment rollback.
- `rollback()` and `sweep()` reject an existing Database context. They open the outermost synchronous transaction, execute a write statement before any ownership query or filesystem operation, and never rely on deferred-transaction read snapshots as a lock.
- A blob/metadata deletion uses a lease-owned recovery directory and hard-link backups. Hard links provide recoverability, not cross-filesystem atomicity: any unlink or restore failure keeps the lease row and complete available recovery evidence and returns the combined error. Deletion statistics change only after both final paths were actually removed.
- Project deletion cannot rely on a foreign-key cascade to erase a live writer's lease. The attachment ownership boundary must settle or reject live leases before the project runtime root or project row is removed.

The reviewer also rejected the hidden direct-write contract. The production inventory contains 18 `AttachmentStore.write()` / `writeFromPath()` call sites across Task creation/messages, Session prompts and tool results, Model Context Protocol (MCP) materialization, graphical user interface screenshots, Build repair/feedback, Frontend Design, Visual Quality Assurance (QA), and multimodal tool output. The ordinary write API must be removed. Every materialization returns an explicit handle and is retained by the exact durable owner transaction or rolled back by its caller. A successful long-lived process must not accumulate invisible lease rows, hard links, or pending directories while waiting for a startup-only sweep.

Required interleaving evidence now includes: two real processes writing the same object; sweep-first and writer-first SQLite ordering; process termination after lease commit, partial blob, blob publication, metadata publication, final unlink, restore, and SQLite commit; outer transaction rollback after `retain(tx)`; nested rollback/sweep rejection; Windows sharing failures; restore failure evidence; PID reuse with a different process token; `EPERM` and unknown liveness probes; different-home root-authority rejection before blob touch; a forced short-directory-key collision; no lease growth after successful retained writes; and project deletion racing a live writer. The implementation may claim process-crash recovery only; it must not claim whole-machine power-loss atomicity while SQLite uses `synchronous=NORMAL` and attachment files are not explicitly synced.

- Confirmed first blocker: runtime project bootstrap performs package discovery only and does not release payloads, which is correct because discovery must be read-only and payload release must be explicit. The explicit HTTP route and Overlay `releaseExpertSquadPayload()` client exist, but no production UI calls that client. Therefore an empty project exposes only already installed packages and gives an ordinary user no explicit way to provision the bundled external `goal-development` package. Historical project-open auto-release records are superseded by the current explicit-provisioning boundary and must not be restored.
- Required correction is one explicit Overlay provisioning command that calls the existing release route, reports installed/skipped results, and refreshes the same project/session catalog. It must not add an implicit startup write, a second package installer, an active-squad field, or an overwrite path. The exact UI action and its error/scope behavior require focused tests and independent review before use as E2E evidence.
- After provisioning is reachable, the existing main backend/database instance must prove project activation through `PATCH /config` with only `prompt_profile.active`, Mission creation with that profile, resolver projection of dynamic agent IDs, a real `dispatch_agent` worker invocation, active catalog/tool/skill mounts, inactive isolation, visible messages, terminal persistence, and a Node Playwright screenshot of the actual served Overlay UI.

#### Real-chain issue ledger

This ledger remains append-only for the current E2E iteration. A problem is removed from the active queue only after root-cause correction, focused regression, real-chain replay, and independent review; green lower-level tests alone do not close an entry.

#### Superseded historical real expert-squad benchmark contract

This entire random-port, isolated-project benchmark contract is retained only as rejected historical design evidence. It must not be executed or treated as current acceptance; the later main-backend/main-database publication constraint and ordinary public Task submission replace it.

- Task definition: from a fresh isolated Project and portable home, use the actual served Overlay UI to explicitly release payload packages, select `goal-development`, wake a Mission, create one real Task, and observe the Task Orchestrator dispatch a real `implementation-engineer` dynamic worker that writes `expert-squad-e2e.txt` with exact requested content and reaches a terminal completed Task state.
- Input: explicit `OPENCORVUS_MODELS_PATH`, explicit `OPENCORVUS_E2E_MODEL`, the selected provider's existing environment credentials, repository source, and the built-in payload source. The harness does not copy auth, discover a model by guessing, read `.env` through swallowed errors, or reuse the user's running server.
- Output: an isolated Project/home, JSON report, settings-after-release screenshot, terminal Task screenshot, exact delivered file, Mission and Task IDs, catalog/mount projections, Task conversation, and dynamic worker session evidence under `.scratch/expert-squad-real-e2e/<run-id>/`.
- Runtime: the Bun parent builds Overlay, initializes a fresh Git project, sets the isolated home/config before dynamically importing production modules, and starts the real `Server` on an operating-system-assigned loopback port with `randomPort=true`. A separate Node process owns Playwright and the actual browser; it opens the same Server's `/ui/`. The parent stops only this Server/browser run and reports every cleanup failure.
- Timeout: build and Node-driver supervision use stdout/stderr inactivity deadlines. Browser/API phases reset their own idle deadline only when the catalog, Work Ledger, Mission messages, Task status, invocation Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG), or transcript signature changes. There is no total wall-clock deadline.
- UI acceptance: `/ui/` must report the freshly built `directory` serving source; the visible browser is non-headless; the initial settings catalog lacks Goal Development; the production `expert-squad-release-payload` button installs it without replace; the user visibly activates Goal Development for the Project and selects `expert-squad:goal-development` in the actual composer; Mission submission is performed through `mission-composer-input` and `mission-composer-submit`; screenshots are captured from the actual rendered page and inspected after the run.
- Runtime acceptance: Project config, Mission session, and Task root session all expose `prompt_profile.active=goal-development`; their catalogs report `active.effective=goal-development`; `active_agent_projection` contains `implementation-engineer` as the dynamic `agent_id` with `base_role=build`; the persisted Task conversation `agentView.sessions` contains `agentID=implementation-engineer` and contains no `agentID=build`.
- Resource acceptance: explicit payload release also installs inactive `opentest`, but the active catalog and `/skill/mounts` contain no MirrorTest projected agent, skill, or tool refs. Goal Development's selector skill and exact projected agent list remain visible through the canonical resolver-backed surfaces.
- Completion acceptance: the Task is `completed`, the implementation worker has visible persisted messages and terminal session evidence, no page/console/backend error is hidden, and `expert-squad-e2e.txt` exactly matches the request. The benchmark does not add an Integrity verdict gate to `complete_task`; complete legacy-team review is a later external-team scenario after this minimum real chain is stable.
- Sources and call points reread before implementation: expert-squad creator skill/checklist; this Recall; payload/manager/registry/resolver/catalog/mount routes; `Server.listen` random-port contract; `InstanceBootstrap` task-loop registration; Overlay browser settings storage, file-menu settings path, provisioning button, composer intent selector, Mission wake service, Work Ledger Task selection, Task conversation/agent rail; Mission benchmark activity polling; and `SessionWake` message persistence.
- Independent harness review rejected reusing `mission-e2e.ts` because it bypasses HTTP/UI and forbids dispatch. It also rejected `mission-benchmark.ts` auth copy, its swallowed report-write error, and benchmark `env.ts` model/provider fallbacks. The accepted implementation shape is an explicitly invoked benchmark outside default test discovery, with fresh state, explicit model catalog/model, canonical APIs, Node-owned Playwright, and exact cleanup evidence.
- The first exact harness review returned `NOT ACCEPT` for five concrete pre-run defects: Session config was read from the wrong response level; API errors reset the idle timer; page request/HTTP failures were invisible; parent timeout did not own the Node/Chrome process tree; and UI operations inherited fixed Playwright elapsed timeouts. Subsequent review also rejected reuse of an existing evidence root, selector assertions satisfiable only by inactive packages, an elapsed `uiStep` timer, and failure to prove Mission Task uniqueness.
- The corrected parent uses the production `runProcessWithInactivityTimeout`/`ProcessSupervisor`, creates an exclusive run-ID directory under the configured evidence parent, and gives the Node driver an extra cleanup-settlement minute after the driver's own idle deadline. The driver fails immediately on API errors; records page, console, request, and HTTP failures; disables Playwright elapsed defaults; resets each UI phase only at named DOM/user-command/screenshot milestones; binds the exact Goal Development selector and `dispatch_agent`; and rechecks exactly one Mission-owned Task in both Work Ledger and Project Board.
- Final pre-run independent review returned `ACCEPT` for parent blob `1d11c0efec0d81a9ba51cc21792c0a5317c65c65` and Node driver blob `71eca5d10943673861dc8bbc088999511513328e`. Node syntax, OpenCorvus typecheck, and scoped diff checks pass. This is only permission to run the benchmark; it is not real-chain acceptance.

First E2E-01 independent review evidence: production call-point inspection found no implicit release and confirmed the action captures its exact scope, uses the sole release route, sends no overwrite option, and ignores stale-scope completion. The review nevertheless returned `NOT ACCEPT` because the passing Node browser test began with `frontend-replica` and `backend`, mocked `installed=[]` plus one skipped package, and refreshed the unchanged catalog. It also lacked release failure and delayed scope-switch behavior. These are test-evidence defects rather than permission to weaken the production scope checks; all four must be covered before the next review.

Second E2E-01 independent review returned scoped `ACCEPT`. The source/surface test passed 6/6 with 116 assertions; the Node browser runner passed 4/4. The reviewer verified a `general`-only catalog through the production button to released `goal-development` visibility; a selected replace checkbox still produced an empty body, no `Content-Type`, and only the captured `directory` query; a 500 release produced a visible action error and no success; and a delayed session-scope release followed by a project-scope switch produced no stale success while the current project catalog independently refreshed without a `sessionID`. The review covers only the expert-squad provisioning hunks; unrelated WorkLedger translation changes in the same locale files remain outside this result.

The first E2E-02/E2E-03 propagation review returned `NOT ACCEPT` even though session/project lineage, explicit gateway authority, dynamic profile propagation, and parent Task preservation were otherwise correct. Its remaining concrete defect was E2E-05: Mission provenance and title were validated after the optional queue Question, while both negative tests forced `queue: false`. The correction validates the server-owned Mission session metadata and semantic title immediately after caller-session lineage and before attachments or Question interaction; the normalized validated title is the value passed to Task creation. Both negative tests now omit `queue` and bind zero calls to `Question.askAndFormat` and `EngineService.createTask`.

Post-correction evidence pending final independent acceptance: actor provenance passes 15/15 with 47 assertions; the complete gateway route file passes 19/19 with 77 assertions, including a real `POST /gateway/control/action` request whose project config selects a non-`general` dynamic squad; OpenCorvus typecheck and the scoped diff check pass. The final review is bound to `panel.ts` blob `2f38fd9640530fb142da738ec71f187c9ae87854`, `task-proposal-tool.ts` blob `edffe63d6e1580e36a0a3d2962888cc8fde5f590`, actor regression blob `86f5d71980c70bdc2c7eaa045665d806c3cdb9e2`, tools regression blob `9f8accd8b4df710244a70a2aa5b9c594f5242b5b`, and gateway regression blob `9bf386f320d5a5f3f464c38a0b222dc2648cdfd3`. Until that review returns, E2E-02, E2E-03, and E2E-05 remain open.

The final E2E-02/E2E-03/E2E-05 independent review returned scoped `ACCEPT` for the blobs above. It independently reran actor plus Gateway at 34/34 with 124 assertions and proposal positive plus polluted-lineage at 2/2 with 11 assertions. It confirmed one `promptProfile -> prompt_profile.active` propagation contract, explicit sessionless Gateway authority, current-project/root lineage, validation before Question, and no metadata/base-role alias or second active field. This acceptance does not cover real Task persistence or worker dispatch because the Gateway route regression mocks `EngineService.createTask`.

E2E-06 independent review returned scoped `ACCEPT` for `panel.test.ts` blob `0ad38afee7db8eda067b9693b3c5b9a8971ba29d` and Mission route test blob `874d1213f62d78a990e9fbc078d47fd9b6bd18e7`. Panel wake positive/negative pass 2/2; the Mission route author contract passes 1/1 with 10 assertions; real SessionWake passes 13/13 with 67 assertions; and the scoped diff check passes. The reviewer explicitly rejected calling the entire Panel file green: E2E-07 and E2E-08 still fail for different recorded causes. A duplicate mocked route-to-wake integration test was not an entry prerequisite because the then-planned isolated E2E was expected to inspect that cross-layer path; the later main-database publication constraint supersedes that planned environment.

E2E-41 final independent review returned scoped `ACCEPT` for the explicit panel-surface lineage. The reviewer bound `tool/wait.ts` `c06b48b1`, `scheduler/cron-service.ts` `64ad90c0`, `scheduler/cron.sql.ts` `cfda7472`, `server/routes/experimental.ts` `ed91e2d3`, and their exact tests. Cron passed 25/25 with 85 assertions, WaitTool 11/11 with 68, route/contract 4/4 with 116, typecheck and scoped diff-check passed. This acceptance proves one typed `PanelSurface` path from tool context through the durable session-only cron row to `SessionWake`; task waits, ordinary cron and no-surface waits remain surface-less. ### 2026-07-13 Exact Model Preflight Review Rejection

The first exact-model slice passed its 17 focused tests with 59 assertions, OpenCorvus typecheck, Node syntax and scoped formatting checks, but the independent blob-bound review returned `REJECT`. The exact provider/model-key and ID checks, one allowed credential name, nonempty credential, capabilities and minimum limits were correct. The failure was the proof boundary: `preflightExactE2EModel` imported `ModelsDev` before isolated runtime paths existed. That import evaluates `Global`, whose top level creates data/config/state/log/bin directories and can clear the active cache. This means a wrong model literal, missing catalog or absent credential could mutate the user's real runtime before being rejected.

The previous `read before -> ModelsDev.get() -> read after` design was also not an atomic catalog proof. `ModelsDev.Data` is lazy-cached, so validation can consume an older parsed object while the digest describes current bytes; an A-to-B-to-A replacement can make both reads equal while the parsed object came from B. The harness then pointed runtime back at the mutable source catalog, leaving a second check/use gap. Finally, the generic Git and Overlay build helper spread the credential-bearing parent environment even though only the backend model process needs `HEXIN_API_KEY`; the accepted browser allowlist therefore did not close the whole child-process boundary.

The replacement call-point disposition is:

| Call point                                                                                                | Disposition                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `src/provider/models.ts` model/provider/catalog schemas and `parseCatalog`                                | Move schema and parser ownership once into a pure production catalog module. `ModelsDev.Model` and `ModelsDev.Provider` remain exported views of that single schema for existing config/provider callers; no duplicate validator is retained.                                                                      |
| `ModelsDev.Data`                                                                                          | Read one catalog snapshot through the pure API and return its parsed catalog. Lazy runtime caching may remain, but the snapshot parser and digest no longer consult that cache.                                                                                                                                    |
| `ModelsDev.refresh` and `refreshHexinProvider`                                                            | Reuse the same pure parser before writing. Their explicit refresh behavior remains unchanged.                                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `expert-squad-real-e2e-model-preflight.ts`                                                                | Validate the exact requested literal and credential presence first, resolve the explicitly supplied path, then read one byte buffer whose JSON parse, production schema parse and SHA-256 digest are inseparable. Return nonsecret evidence plus the validated bytes; import no runtime-global module.             |
| `expert-squad-real-e2e.ts`                                                                                | After successful preflight creates the run scope, write the validated bytes to one isolated catalog path and point runtime at that immutable run-owned copy before importing logger/server/Instance/Database. Report the source path, isolated runtime path and one digest without another model-selection source. |
| Generic Git/build child and browser supervisor child                                                      | Consume one shared explicit operating-environment projector. Git/build receive no provider credential, model selector or benchmark source data; the browser additionally receives only its exact nonsecret scenario inputs. There is no ambient merge or redaction-after-inheritance path.                         |
| Existing `ModelsDev.get`, config schemas, provider discovery, CLI auth/refresh and provider route callers | Keep their public call shape and consume the refactored `ModelsDev` exports. No caller receives a second catalog path, parser or alias.                                                                                                                                                                            |

Fresh-process regressions must execute the actual harness import path with an isolated non-existent home/config/evidence scope. Wrong exact literal, missing path and malformed catalog must exit before any of those resource paths is created and must never emit the credential sentinel. Snapshot behavior must prove that a later source-file mutation cannot change the already parsed model/digest/bytes, and that the isolated runtime copy hashes to the same digest. A real child process launched with the shared projector must observe required operating variables and explicit fixture inputs while both `HEXIN_API_KEY` and an unrelated secret sentinel are absent.
